gaps.why_now: A dedicated Phase 11 build entry now keeps the landed gpio_wdt starter and the survey checkpoint reviewable together instead of letting the lane drift after the first driver scaffold landed.
The survey gate now acts as a freshness check around the landed gpio_wdt starter so the lane does not drift back to pre-driver assumptions or overclaim broader watchdog progress.

The survey note now records the landed gpio_wdt starter, the direct platform-driver shell, the probe-summary follow-up, the nowayout-aware teardown-facing stop helper, the explicit teardown summary for disable ordering and failure-mode fallout, the metadata-only registration plan, the first bounded register-device call summary, and the current hardware-validation posture so the remaining Phase 11 gap stays explicit without overclaiming broader watchdog progress.

The first gpio_wdt starter is now landed and models hw_algo parsing, heartbeat margin validation, an explicit watchdog metadata summary, the tiny platform-driver shell, bounded start or stop or ping transitions, a tiny probe-time summary, a nowayout-aware teardown-facing stop helper, an explicit teardown summary for disable ordering and failure-mode fallout, a metadata-only registration plan, and the first bounded register-device call summary without touching live GPIO or platform registration.

Dedicated Phase 11 tests now keep the toggle and level state transitions, heartbeat validation, direct watchdog metadata, starter-local nowayout policy bookkeeping, always-running stop behavior, teardown-facing nowayout outcomes, explicit disable-order teardown checks, registration handoff bookkeeping, and the first bounded register-device request honest around the landed simple-driver scaffold.

A bounded slice note records exactly what the gpio_wdt starter, direct platform-driver shell, probe-summary helper, teardown-facing stop helper, explicit teardown summary, metadata-only registration plan, and register-device call summary cover so later Phase 11 work can extend the model without reopening the starter contract.

The first bounded hardware-validation matrix now names the shared Phase 11 replay path, the property and transition evidence, the teardown-facing stop evidence, the explicit teardown-summary evidence, the starter-local nowayout policy proof, the explicit remaining blocker surface, and the first bounded register-device call surface that keep the gpio_wdt packet reviewable without claiming live GPIO or watchdog-core execution.

The starter now keeps the direct watchdog-info contract explicit through `watchdogMetadataSummary()` so review can see the `GPIO Watchdog` identity, the bounded `WDIOF_SETTIMEOUT`, `WDIOF_MAGICCLOSE`, and `WDIOF_KEEPALIVEPING` surface, and the starter-local ops readiness before descriptor-backed registration work lands.

The starter now keeps the tiny platform-driver shell explicit through `platformDriverIdentitySummary()` so review can see the `gpio-wdt` driver name, the `linux,wdt-gpio` OF match entry, the `gpio_wdt_probe()` callback, and the default `module_platform_driver()` versus `CONFIG_GPIO_WATCHDOG_ARCH_INITCALL` override boundary without claiming live registration.

The lane now lands a tiny probe-time summary for always-running startup, requested GPIO line mode, and watchdog-core-facing bookkeeping so the starter describes more of gpio_wdt_probe() before any live GPIO or platform glue.

The starter now lands a tiny nowayout-aware stop helper plus an explicit teardown summary so review can distinguish watchdog-core stop blocking from hardware always-running behavior, preserve teardown-facing stop outcomes, and keep disable ordering reviewable before any live GPIO or platform glue.

The starter now adds a tiny registration-facing handoff summary so review can see whether startup state, stop policy, timeout init, and reboot bookkeeping reach watchdog-core registration before any live GPIO or platform glue.

The starter now records the first chosen registration surface and validation focus so review can see that the lane is still limited to watchdog-device metadata planning rather than a real `devm_watchdog_register_device()` call or live GPIO glue.

The starter now adds one tiny register-device request summary so review can see the exact watchdog metadata, timeout, nowayout, parent, stop-on-reboot, and teardown-adjacent startup state that would reach the first bounded `devm_watchdog_register_device()` request before any live GPIO descriptor acquisition or reboot glue lands.

The starter now adds one tiny `registerDeviceFailureSummary()` helper so review can see the remaining descriptor preflight, platform-registration, and reboot-glue blockers as an explicit parked failure surface instead of inferring them from the bounded register-device request alone.

Platform-driver registration, GPIO descriptor acquisition, watchdog core registration, and reboot integration remain blocked even after the register-device call summary and explicit remaining-blocker summary land because the lane still lacks a live descriptor-backed probe path and a richer hardware-validation plan.
